note: Two different measures, kept apart. 14.b.1 is a self-reported policy score for about 190 countries; IHH is tonnes of catch under each kind of rule for 51 countries. Neither is a substitute for the other.

sdg14b1.source: UN SDG Global Database (UN Statistics Division); custodian agency FAO; data from country self-reporting in the CCRF questionnaire
sdg14b1.licence: Not stated in the API response; cite as UN SDG Global Database, indicator 14.b.1.
sdg14b1.description: Degree of application of a legal/regulatory/policy/institutional framework which recognizes and protects access rights for small-scale fisheries (level of implementation: 1 lowest to 5 highest)
sdg14b1.scale_footnote: Level of implementation: 1 lowest to 5 highest

levels.1: Very low implementation of instruments for access to resources and markets for small-scale fisheries
levels.2: Low implementation of instruments for access to resources and markets for small-scale fisheries
levels.3: Medium implementation of instruments for access to resources and markets for small-scale fisheries
levels.4: High implementation of instruments for access to resources and markets for small-scale fisheries
levels.5: Very high implementation of instruments for access to resources and markets for small-scale fisheries

Observation Status.L: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

notes: What is scored: three questions from FAO's Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries (CCRF) questionnaire, answered by each country's fisheries administration. (1) laws, regulations, policies, plans or strategies that specifically target small-scale fisheries, weight 0.4; (2) ongoing initiatives to implement the SSF Guidelines, weight 0.3; (3) an advisory or consultative body in which fishers and fish workers can take part, weight 0.3. The 0-1 total is reported only as a band, 1-5. (Metadata 4.a-4.c.)
It measures whether frameworks exist on paper and are being applied, not how much catch or how many fishers they cover. It cannot say who actually holds access rights on the water.

Self-reported. The metadata itself warns of self-report bias: countries tend to report 'a better reality' than the one in place (Metadata section 6). 'Blank' and 'unknown' answers are scored as 'no' (Metadata 4.c).

European Union member states are scored from the EU's single response, not their own; the API footnote says 'Indicator developped upon responses provided by the EU'. Those rounds are listed in eu_derived_rounds and counted in latest_eu_derived: a block of identical scores that is really one answer. The same footnote also appears on some non-members (see eu_footnote_anomalies); those scores are kept as published and the footnote is treated as a likely error in the source.
Some landlocked countries report on their inland fisheries, although target 14.b is about marine resources (Metadata 4.b).
A null score means no score was published for that round - never zero. The API's reason is kept in round_detail[year].missing; missing_reasons counts them.
Regional and other groupings (World, Africa, SIDS, LDCs and so on) are in the same API series; they are dropped here and listed in dropped_aggregates.

ihh_governance.data_description: Governance data for marine and inland small-scale fisheries for 51 country case studies (28 for marine and inland, 17 marine only, 6 inland only). Note that this number is less than the total of 58 country-case studies covered for catch because only 51 country case studies provided governance data.
ihh_governance.unit: Catch is in tonnes (live weight equivalent). Presence is indicated by a 1 and absence by a 0.

license.name: License
license.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case licenses are used as a criteria to grant access, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to them.
license.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

historical_use.name: Historical use
historical_use.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case historical use is used as a criteria to grant access, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to it.
historical_use.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

residence.name: Place of residence
residence.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case place of residence is used as a criteria to grant access, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to it.
residence.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

registration.name: Vessel registration
registration.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case vessel registration is used as a criteria to grant access, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to it.
registration.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

open_acc.name: Open access
open_acc.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case there is open access, country catch estimate (in tonnes) with open access.
open_acc.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

no_info.name: No information on access
no_info.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. Country catch estimate (in tonnes) for which no information was available.
no_info.sheet_block: SSF Access strategies (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

vessels.name: Vessel restrictions
vessels.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case there are vessel restrictions, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to them.
vessels.sheet_block: SSF Harvesting management measures (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

tac.name: TAC (Total Allowable Catch)
tac.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case there are TACs, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to them.
tac.sheet_block: SSF Harvesting management measures (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

size.name: Restriction on the size of the harvested species
size.definition: Presence (1) or absence (0) information. In case there are size limits, country catch estimate (in tonnes) subjected to them.
size.sheet_block: SSF Harvesting management measures (they are not mutually exclusive, i.e. there is double counting)

concepts.Catch: It refers to "nominal catch”, which is defined as the live weight equivalent of the landings (i.e. landings on a round, fresh basis; landings on a round, whole basis; or landings on an ex-water weight basis), excluding discards.
concepts.Small-scale fisheries: The definition of small-scale fisheries varies considerably in different countries, but generally includes low-technology, low-capital, labour-intensive fishing practices. Often, the term artisanal is used to refer to small-scale fisheries. For the purpose of country and territory case study data collection, the most common definition (e.g. legal or operational) for small-scale fisheries in each country or territory was used.
concepts.Devolution of rights: Refers to when fishing authorities grant management, exclusion and/or transferability (also called withdrawal) rights to individuals, groups and/or communities over the catch or any other aspect of the fishery as well (based on Schlager and Ostrom, 1992).
concepts.Access: The right to enter a defined physical property. In this case a body of water where fishing will take place
concepts.Management: The right to regulate internal use patterns and transform the resource by making improvements.
concepts.Exclusion: The right to determine who will have an access right, and how that right may be transferred.
concepts.Transferability (Alienation): The right to sell or lease either or both of the above collective choice rights.

groups.access: How access to fish is granted. Not mutually exclusive: one tonne can be under a licence and historical use at once, so shares can add to more than 100%.
groups.harvest_rules: Harvesting management measures in force. Not mutually exclusive.
groups.rights: Which rights are devolved to fishers (devolved rights, analysis I). Not mutually exclusive: a tonne under management and exclusion rights counts in both.
groups.engagement: How engaged fishers are in management (filed under devolved rights, analysis I, in the workbook). Not mutually exclusive.
groups.rights_breakdown: Devolved rights, analysis II: every tonne is in exactly one category, so catch_t adds up to the total and pct to about 100%.

output_fields.catch_t: Workbook column 'National_catch_average (in tonnes)' (Small-scale fisheries average catch): Average catch for small-scale fisheries at the country level was determined by summing the annual catch (2013-2017) and then calculating the average for the available years.
output_fields.flag: Workbook column 'Flag'. 'E' = estimate ("Observation obtained through an estimation methodology").
output_fields.<group>.<field>.present: The field's presence column: true = 1, false = 0.
output_fields.<group>.<field>.catch_t: The field's tonnes column; null where the workbook says 'NA'.
output_fields.<group>.<field>.pct: catch_t / the row's catch_t x 100, one decimal. Computed here.
output_fields.devolved_any: Computed here: catch under at least one devolved right (analysis II).
output_fields.notes: Row-level warnings found while reading this row.

notes: Coverage: 51 countries - 28 with marine and inland rows, 17 marine only, 6 inland only. The workbook's metadata says: "51 country and territory case studies (CCS), 28 for marine and inland, 17 marine only, 6 inland only."
Every 'pct' is computed by this script: that row's tonnes as a share of the same row's catch_t (marine and inland are never mixed). Tonnes are the workbook's own values.
devolved_any is computed by this script: the sum of the seven analysis II categories in which at least one right is devolved (everything except no_rights and not_gov_info).

Time: the workbook says "Governance arrangements information: 2019-2020. Catch data: 2013-2017." - so catch is a 2013-2017 average and the rules are those recorded in 2019-2020. Flags used: E ('E' = estimate).

Ambiguity: the metadata's description of 'no_rights' is a copy of the high-engagement one ("In case there is high engagement ..."). Its NAME, 'No rights devolved to fishers', and its place in the mutually exclusive analysis II are taken as its meaning.
Ambiguity: management's tonnes column is headed 'mgmt_catch.x', not 'mgmt_catch'. It is read as the tonnes for the 'mgmt' field; the '.x' suffix is not explained in the workbook.

Ambiguity: the engagement fields are defined only by their names (e.g. 'High engagement of fishers in management'); the workbook does not say what they are a share of. In this data they only appear where management rights do and never exceed management tonnes, so they read as engagement within catch that has management rights. The levels overlap - engagement tonnes add to more than the management tonnes in 17 rows (BRA inland, COG marine, KEN inland, KEN marine, MDG inland, MDG marine, MWI inland, MEX marine, MOZ inland, MOZ marine, PHL inland, PHL marine, LKA marine, THA inland, THA marine, VNM marine, ZMB inland) - so they are not a breakdown.

'no_info' (no information on access) and 'not_gov_info' (no information on devolved rights) answer different questions; their tonnes differ in 10 rows (BRA marine, GAB inland, GMB inland, GMB marine, GNB marine, IND marine, LAO inland, NOR marine, ZAF inland, ZAF marine).

Where a field is present but its tonnage is 'NA' in the workbook, catch_t and pct are null and that row's notes list the fields. Rows affected: ARG inland, BRA marine, COG inland, GAB inland, GHA inland, GHA marine, IND marine, SYC marine.

Scope, from the workbook: only formally devolved rights are counted - "The analysis does not include governance regimes with informally devolved rights" - so customary arrangements are not in these numbers.
The workbook's country name cell is blank for GBR; the UN M49 name is used instead.
